author: Ananya Chetia
title: New terrorism-related charges filed against man accused of shooting two Israeli Embassy staffers - NewsBreak
text:
By Ananya Chetia ,
1 hours ago U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro announced that 31-year-old Elias Rodriguez from Chicago, was charged in a 13-count superseding indictment unsealed with multiple terrorism-related offenses in connection after two Israeli Embassy staff members outside the Capital Jewish Museum were shot and killed in D.C.
The man was previously charged with the murder of a foreign official through a firearm, discharging a firearm during a crime violence, two federal counts of hate crime resulting in death and two counts each of first-degree premeditated murder while armed and assault with intent to kill while armed under the D.C criminal code.
He now has four additional counts of acts of terrorism while armed.

“My office will not rest in our efforts to hold Elias Rodriguez accountable for this horrific, and targeted act of terror against Yaron Lischinsky, Sarah Milgrim and our Jewish community,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “These additional terrorism-related charges carry a mandatory life sentence under D.C. Code, while also reflecting the reality that this act was in fact an act of terror.”
“In addition to allegedly murdering two innocent people and terrorizing the survivors of his attack at the Capital Jewish Museum, Rodriguez wrote and published a manifesto attempting to morally justify his actions and inspire others to commit political violence,” said FBI Assistant Director in Charge Darren B. Cox of the Washington Field Office. “His alleged actions warrant the additional terrorism charges being announced today.”
The 31-year-old is accused of shooting Israeli Embassy staff members Yaron Lischinsky, 30, and Sarah Milgrim, 26, with a semi-automatic handgun on May 2025. Officials said Rodriguez fired roughly 20 shots.
The attorney office noted that Rodriguez said “Free Palestine.” After he entered the museum, where the two victims previously were, he said, “I did it for Palestine. I did it for Gaza,” the attorney’s office wrote.
Lischinsky, an Israeli citizen, and Milgrim from Kansas were to be engaged to one another. Lischinsky bought an engagement ring with plans to propose to Milgrim a week later, according to the Israeli ambassador to the United States, Yechiel Leiter.
BI’s Washington Field Office and the Metropolitan Police Department are investigating the case. The attorney’s office noted it is being prosecuted by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia with assistance from the Civil Rights Division of the Department of Justice.
President Donald Trump condemned the shooting in May on a Truth Social post.
“These horrible D.C. killings, based obviously on antisemitism, must end, NOW! Hatred and Radicalism have no place in the USA. Condolences to the families of the victims. So sad that such things as this can happen! God Bless You ALL!”
summary: 1 hours ago U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro announced that 31-year-old Elias Rodriguez from Chicago, was charged in a 13-count superseding indictment unsealed with multiple terrorism-related offenses in connection after two Israeli Embassy staff members outside the Capital Jewish Museum were shot and killed in D.C.
